I bought this game in 2024, loved it even it has been out for more than half a decade. Definitely one of the best sandbox ww2 games! I got possessed with immersing myself into the greatest war of man kind. Excellent graphics and epic sound effects!

Cons :
- Multiplayer Game is unbalanced (There is no Team Auto Balance or switch team like in BF3, if 50% of your team Quits you'll still have the same amount of team members on the next round)
- Lots of Hackers/Cheaters (Like a lot of them)
- Planes can "Disappear" from view when they fly up high enough thus making them impossible for Anti Air to spot them (No I did not find a setting to increase the Render Distance).
- Hurr Durr "Don't like it, don't buy it" (I got it on discount and because a friend wanted to play, wouldn't have bought it otherwise)
- FireStorm (Their Battle Royale Game mode) is dead at least for the Asia region, only had 8 players (Including us) playing the last time we played it

Pros :
- Haha there's Bobs and Vagene in the game

I played the single player campaigns, and in my opinion they're epic. the scenery is beautiful, the missions feel meaningful, challenging and heartwarming at times. I really enjoyed the ability to have multiple approaches to a mission, and allowing you to really function as a stealth player if you so choose (or not) and give you the feel of being challenged, not knowing where the enemy is and the need to scout your environment. One aspect of the game that maybe could've been better, though admittedly i exploited a lot in the game is the near total lack of intelligence of the enemy. They see a dead soldier, but so long as they didn't see them get shot, no alarms are raised, and all continues as normal, so you can literally stack 3-5 stealth kills as each soldier comes to quietly investigate the murder before going on their business. This could've definitely been done better. Some more than others, however overall I think the designers did a great job in giving the characters you play a soul, a personality, an internal battle of their own. Thoroughly enjoyed this game.

Battlefield V is a damn rollercoaster. When it works, it’s absolutely amazing — explosions everywhere, chaotic firefights, and those “holy shit” moments that only Battlefield can pull off. The sound design hits hard, the movement feels smooth as hell, and some maps are straight-up gorgeous.

But then the game decides to piss you off.

The time-to-kill feels like it changes every other match, hit-reg likes to take a nap whenever it wants, and sometimes you die to stuff that makes you question your entire existence. And don’t even get me started on the random bugs — they show up like uninvited guests and ruin the vibe.

Overall? Battlefield V is a badass game wrapped in a messy package. When it’s good, it slaps. When it’s not, it makes you want to slam your keyboard through the table.

Battlefield V is a visually stunning first-person shooter that immerses players in the chaos of World War II. With its realistic graphics, dynamic environments, and intense multiplayer modes, the game offers a compelling experience for fans of tactical combat. The campaign mode provides a gripping narrative, highlighting lesser-known stories from the war, while the multiplayer features large-scale battles with destructible terrain and a variety of classes and vehicles. The game’s emphasis on teamwork and strategy makes each match engaging and unpredictable. Additionally, Battlefield V introduces innovative features like the Tides of War live service, which keeps content fresh and players engaged over time. Overall, Battlefield V combines immersive gameplay, impressive visuals, and strategic depth to deliver a top-tier military shooter experience.
